summary: An Arabic question with a question word puts that word first and leaves the rest of the sentence as it is: no helper verb, no inversion, no هَلْ, and ؟ at the end — تَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَةَ → مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ؟ (What do you drink?). The words: مَا (what, before a noun or pronoun) and مَاذَا (what, before a verb), مَنْ (who), أَيْنَ (where), مَتَى (when), كَيْفَ (how), لِمَاذَا (why, “for what”), كَمْ (how many, how much — followed by a singular noun in the accusative: كَمْ أَخًا؟), أَيّ (which — followed by a genitive noun, and it declines itself: أَيُّ / أَيَّ / أَيِّ) and لِمَنْ (whose, “to whom”). A preposition goes in front of the question word: مِنْ أَيْنَ؟ إِلَى أَيْنَ؟ مَعَ مَنْ؟ بِكَمْ؟ With a noun no “is” is needed: أَيْنَ الطَّبِيبُ؟ مَتَى الْعَشَاءُ؟ — and the answer about a job is verbless too: مَنْ هُوَ؟ هُوَ طَبِيبٌ (he is a doctor), هِيَ طَبِيبَةٌ (she is a doctor).

blocks.caption: The question word comes first; the rest keeps the order of the statement.

items.title: Question
points: مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ؟ — the object becomes مَاذَا
مَتَى تَأْكُلُ الْغَدَاءَ؟ — the verb does not move

blocks.title: كَمْ + a singular noun in the accusative.
blocks.text: كَمْ أَخًا عِنْدَكَ؟ (how many brothers?) — not *كَمْ إِخْوَةً؟. The noun is singular, indefinite and accusative (-an): كَمْ كِتَابًا؟ كَمْ أُخْتًا؟. For a price add بِ: بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ (how much is this?).

head: place of أَيّ
form
example
rows: أَيُّ بَيْتٍ بَيْتُكَ؟ (which house is yours?)
أَيَّ كِتَابٍ تُرِيدُ؟ (which book do you want?)
مِنْ أَيِّ بَلَدٍ أَنْتَ؟ (which country are you from?)
blocks.caption: أَيّ is the only question word with case endings; the noun after it is always genitive and indefinite.

blocks.title: Never هَلْ with a question word.
blocks.text: هَلْ is only for yes/no questions (lesson 9). *هَلْ أَيْنَ الْمَحَطَّةُ؟ is wrong — say أَيْنَ الْمَحَطَّةُ؟.

blocks.title: Who is she? — She is a doctor.
blocks.text: مَنْ هِيَ؟ هِيَ طَبِيبَةٌ. No word for “is”, no word for “a”: the indefinite noun with -un says “a doctor”. Change the job to the feminine when you speak about a woman: أُمِّي مُمَرِّضَةٌ, أُخْتِي فَنَّانَةٌ.

In speech the question words differ by region — Levant شُو (what), وَيْن (where), لَيْش (why), قَدَّيْش (how much), مِين (who); Egypt إِيه, فِين, لِيه, كَام, مِين. Standard Arabic, used in writing and understood everywhere, has the forms of this page.

askYourself: What am I asking about: a thing (مَا / مَاذَا), a person (مَنْ), a place (أَيْنَ), a time (مَتَى), a way (كَيْفَ), a reason (لِمَاذَا), a number (كَمْ), a choice (أَيّ) or an owner (لِمَنْ)?
“What”: does a verb follow? → مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ؟ A noun or pronoun? → مَا هٰذَا؟
Does the question need a preposition? → put it before the question word: مِنْ أَيْنَ؟ مَعَ مَنْ؟ بِكَمْ؟
After كَمْ: is my noun singular, indefinite and accusative (كَمْ أَخًا)?
After أَيّ: is my noun indefinite and genitive — and does أَيّ take the case of its own place (أَيُّ / أَيَّ / أَيِّ)?
Did I leave out هَلْ, keep the order of the statement and end with ؟?

traps: No inversion and no “do”: مَتَى تَأْكُلُ؟ (lit. when you-eat?).
مَاذَا before a verb, مَا before a noun: *مَاذَا هٰذَا؟ → مَا هٰذَا؟.
*هَلْ مَاذَا …؟ — a question word never takes هَلْ.
كَمْ + singular: كَمْ أَخًا؟, not *كَمْ إِخْوَةً؟ — and accusative: not *كَمْ أَخٌ؟.
أَيّ + indefinite genitive: أَيَّ كِتَابٍ, not *أَيَّ الْكِتَابَ.
مَنْ (man, who) and مِنْ (min, from) are both written من without vowels.
Feminine jobs: هِيَ طَبِيبَةٌ, not *هِيَ طَبِيبٌ.

quiz.why: The question word first, then the statement unchanged; مَاذَا before a verb; never هَلْ with a question word.
After كَمْ the noun is singular, indefinite and accusative: أَخًا.
أَيّ is the object (accusative أَيَّ); the noun after it is indefinite genitive: كِتَابٍ.
“Whose” is “to whom”: لِ + مَنْ. مَنْ alone asks “who”, مِنْ means “from”.

quiz.q: “Who is she? — She is a nurse.”
quiz.why: مَنْ for a person; the job takes the feminine ة for a woman; no word for “is”.

quiz.q: Where does the preposition go in “Where are you from?”
options: before the question word: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟
at the end: أَيْنَ أَنْتَ مِنْ؟
it is left out: أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟
quiz.answer: before the question word: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟
quiz.why: Arabic never strands a preposition: مِنْ أَيْنَ؟ إِلَى أَيْنَ؟ مَعَ مَنْ؟

seeAlso.note: Hebrew question words also come first and are often the same Semitic words: מָה = مَا, מָתַי = مَتَى, כַּמָּה = كَمْ. But Hebrew כַּמָּה takes a plural noun (כַּמָּה אַחִים), Arabic كَمْ a singular accusative (كَمْ أَخًا).

German puts the W-word first and the verb second (Was trinkst du?); Arabic also fronts the question word but never moves the verb. German welcher declines like Arabic أَيّ (welchen Kaffee / أَيَّ قَهْوَةٍ).
Chinese leaves the question word where the answer will stand (你喝什么？ “you drink what?”); Arabic moves it to the front (مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ؟). Chinese 多少 / 几 ask like Arabic كَمْ.
Yes/no questions take هَلْ (lesson 9) — never together with a question word.
